extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), patent office staff, and other parties who correspond or interact with the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules (Title 37 CFR consolidated) governing filing, correspondence, prosecution, reexamination, employee testimony, mask-work proclamations, and related administrative processes at the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.1 Addresses for non-trademark correspondence with the United States Patent and Trademark Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for correspondence submitted via the USPTO electronic filing system in accordance with § 1.6(a)(4), all correspondence intended for the USPTO must be addressed to either 'Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313–1450' or to specific areas within the Office as provided in this section. When appropriate, correspondence should also be marked for the attention of a particular office or individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specific addressing rules and mail-stop markings for patent correspondence (Commissioner for Patents address), PTAB appeals (see §41.10 or §42.6), Office of General Counsel (litigation, disciplinary, Solicitor, General Counsel addresses and warnings about improper address), Office of Public Records (assignment recordation and document services addresses), Office of Enrollment and Discipline (Mail Stop OED), and special markings for PCT ('Mail Stop PCT'), ex parte reexamination ('Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam'), inter partes reexamination ('Mail Stop Inter Partes Reexam'), supplemental examination ('Mail Stop Supplemental Examination'), maintenance-fee correspondence ('Mail Stop Maintenance Fee'), and patent term extension ('Mail Stop Hatch-Waxman PTE'). Includes warning that correspondence improperly addressed to certain PO Boxes may not be filed elsewhere and may be returned. Also notes historical amendments and effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.2 Business to be transacted in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: All business with the Patent and Trademark Office should be transacted in writing. The personal attendance of applicants or their attorneys or agents at the USPTO is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office's action will be based exclusively on the written record. No attention will be paid to any alleged oral promise, stipulation, or understanding in relation to which there is disagreement or doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 1.3 Business to be conducted with decorum and courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct their business with the USPTO with decorum and courtesy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers presented in violation of this requirement may be subject to the Office's rules (implies potential refusal or other administrative action). This is a professional-conduct requirement governing interactions and submissions to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart C — § 104.21 Scope and purpose (Employee testimony and production of documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets forth policies and procedures regarding testimony of USPTO employees as witnesses in legal proceedings and production or disclosure of Office documents pursuant to a demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the subpart's scope, and enumerates exceptions where the subpart does not apply (e.g., employee testimony unrelated to official business, or former employee expert testimony in matters they did not participate in).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 104.22 Demand for testimony or production of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Demands for testimony or production of documents relating to USPTO employees must be addressed to the General Counsel; subpoenas must be served in accordance with Federal Rules and a copy sent to the General Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employee may not give testimony, produce documents, or answer inquiries subject to a demand without General Counsel approval. Every demand (except when the United States is a party) must be accompanied by an affidavit or declaration under 28 U.S.C. 1746 or 35 U.S.C. 25(b) detailing the proceeding, requester interest, reason for demand, why information isn't available elsewhere, intended use of testimony, summary of desired testimony, and why documents can't substitute for testimony. Failure of counsel to cooperate may be grounds for noncompliance; determinations to comply or not comply do not waive other grounds. If General Counsel declines to comply, DOJ representation will be sought and attempts made to quash/modify subpoenas; if DOJ representation unavailable, employee should appear and cite Touhy (United States ex rel. Touhy v. Ragen) and the Office rules. Employees must notify General Counsel immediately when served.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 104.23 Expert or opinion testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on USPTO employees providing expert or opinion testimony: employees shall not provide expert testimony regarding Office information, subjects, or activities except on behalf of the United States or a party represented by the Department of Justice, unless the General Counsel authorizes otherwise under exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authorized, testimony must be limited to facts within the employee's personal knowledge unless exceptional circumstances are shown. If asked on the stand for unapproved expert testimony, the employee must decline, request opportunity to consult with General Counsel, and explain possible approval after consultation. If ordered by tribunal to give such testimony without consultation, the employee should respectfully refuse citing Touhy. If unauthorized expert testimony was given, employee must promptly inform General Counsel and provide a written summary. When the U.S. is a party, employees may not testify as expert witnesses for any party other than the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 104.24 Demands or requests for records protected by confidentiality statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demands in legal proceedings for production of records, or for employee testimony regarding information protected by confidentiality statutes (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 122, Privacy Act, Trade Secrets Act), must satisfy the requirements for disclosure set forth in those statutes and associated rules before records may be provided or testimony given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that confidentiality statutes control disclosure; the Office will enforce statutory protections and associated rules when responding to demands for protected records or testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 104.32 Procedure for requesting indemnification (Employee indemnification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets procedures employees must follow when seeking indemnification for civil actions brought against them for actions within scope of employment: upon being served with process, the employee must deliver process and a detailed report to the General Counsel within five calendar days; requests for indemnification must be submitted through supervisory chain and include documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation includes copies of verdict/judgment/settlement proposals, explanation of how employee was acting within scope of employment, and statement of other indemnification sources (insurance). Failure to timely satisfy initial requirements may preclude consideration; the procedure references FTCA and DOJ regulations for filing administrative claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 104.41 Procedure for filing tort claims; § 104.42 Finality of settlement or denial of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative claims against the Office pursuant to the Federal Tort Claims Act must be filed with the General Counsel per the specified administrative-claims procedures. Only decisions of the Director or General Counsel regarding settlement or denial are final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs claimants to the FTCA provision and corresponding DOJ regulations and notes finality rules for purposes of judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 150 — § 150.1 Definitions (Requests for Presidential proclamations under 17 U.S.C. 902(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms used in Part 150: Director (Under Secretary and Director of USPTO), foreign government, interim order, mask work (series of related images representing semiconductor patterns), Presidential proclamation, request, proceeding, and Secretary (Secretary of Commerce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides precise statutory/administrative definitions that set the scope for subsequent procedural rules (used to interpret requirements for submissions and evaluations under this Part).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 150.2 Initiation of evaluation (for section 902 proclamations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may initiate evaluation of the propriety of recommending issuance, revision, suspension, or revocation of a section 902 proclamation independently or as directed by the Secretary; the Director must initiate evaluation upon receipt of a request from a foreign government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who may initiate and under what triggers (i.e., receipt of a foreign government request) evaluations related to Presidential proclamations extending mask-work registration privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 150.3 Submission of requests (for section 902 proclamations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for issuance of a section 902 proclamation shall be submitted by foreign governments and must include: a copy of the foreign law or legal rulings that provide protection for U.S. mask works; copies of implementing regulations or administrative orders; copies of laws/regulations establishing or regulating registration (if any); any other relevant laws/regulations; all copies must be unedited, full-text, reproduced from original if possible; all material must be in the original language and, if not in English, accompanied by a certified English translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets documentary completeness and translation requirements; emphasizes full-text/unedited documents and certified translations to support the Director's evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 150.4 Evaluation (of requests for section 902 proclamations)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a request (or initiating an evaluation), the Director may publish a Federal Register notice soliciting relevant and material comments on adequacy and effectiveness of foreign protection for U.S. mask works; comments should include detailed explanations and administration issues and must be submitted within 60 days of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If comments raise relevant reasons why a proclamation should not issue, the Director will contact the commenter and the requesting government to attempt resolution; if unresolved, the Director may hold a public hearing. The Director evaluates comments, the request, information from any section 914 (interim order) proceeding and hearings, then forwards evaluation and draft recommendation to the Secretary, who forwards recommendation to the President. Also notes use of section 914 proceeding information when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 150.5 Duration of proclamation; requests for revision, suspension, or revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommendation for issuance of a proclamation may include terms and conditions regarding its duration. Requests for revision, suspension, or revocation of a proclamation may be submitted by any interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for revision/suspension/revocation are handled in substantially the same manner as initial issuance requests, implying similar document and comment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 150.6 Mailing address (for Part 150 submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests and all correspondence pursuant to Part 150 shall be addressed to: Mail Stop Congressional Relations, Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the required mailing address for foreign-government requests and related correspondence; includes historical revision notes.
